Subsamples of individuals

Source: R/sampling.R
subsample_individuals.Rd

Draws a subsample of the individuals of each population of real data, with the sampling schemes of sample_individuals(): a fixed number of individuals per population (n), a share of the individuals (fraction), only the most abundant species of each site (cover), and a minimum number of individuals per population (min_n). It shows how much a result depends on sampling effort, alone or through trait_rarefaction().

Usage

subsample_individuals(
  individuals,
  n = NULL,
  fraction = NULL,
  cover = NULL,
  min_n = 1,
  site = "site",
  species = "species",
  abundance = NULL
)

Arguments

individuals

Data frame with one row per individual.

n

Number of individuals drawn from each population, or NULL to keep all.

fraction

Probability that each individual is kept; used when n is NULL.

cover

Share (0 to 1) of the abundance of each site covered by the species kept, from the most abundant down (Pakeman & Quested 2007), or NULL to keep every species. Abundances are those of the abundance column, or the numbers of individuals in the data. Species tied in abundance are taken in the order of the data, and populations with an abundance of zero are never kept.

min_n

Minimum number of individuals of a population after sampling.

site, species

Names of the columns with the site and the species.

abundance

Name of a column with the abundance of each population (the same value for all its individuals), or NULL to use the numbers of individuals in the data.

Value

The rows of individuals kept, in their original order.

Details

The schemes are applied in this order: species outside cover are removed, individuals are drawn without replacement (n from each population, all of them when the population is smaller, or each one with probability fraction), and populations left with fewer than min_n individuals are removed.

References

Pakeman, R. J., & Quested, H. M. (2007). Sampling plant functional traits: what proportion of the species need to be measured? Applied Vegetation Science, 10, 91–96. doi:10.1111/j.1654-109x.2007.tb00507.x

See also

trait_rarefaction(), sample_individuals().

Examples

set.seed(1)
ind <- data.frame(site = rep(c("s1", "s2"), each = 50),
                  species = sample(c("a", "b", "c"), 100, TRUE, prob = c(6, 3, 1)),
                  trait = rnorm(100))
table(subsample_individuals(ind, n = 5)[c("site", "species")])
#>     species
#> site a b c
#>   s1 5 5 4
#>   s2 5 5 2
# only the species making up 80% of the individuals of each site
table(subsample_individuals(ind, cover = 0.8)[c("site", "species")])
#>     species
#> site  a  b
#>   s1 27 19
#>   s2 30 18
